title: Crash-Cooling Duration Outlier
app: Brewfather batch exports, iSpindel and Tilt hydrometers, ESPHome mash probes, keg pressure sensors, brew-fridge telemetry, and cellar climate data via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=brew:fermentation event=crash_cool
| stats avg(duration_hr) as avg_duration_hr, max(duration_hr) as max_duration_hr by batch_name
| where avg_duration_hr>24 OR max_duration_hr>36
| sort - avg_duration_hr
description: Uses Fermentation crash-cooling events telemetry to monitor how long crash-cooling is taking per batch in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for batches that are cooling slower than the normal process, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest Fermentation crash-cooling events data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a daily cadence.
grandmaExplanation: It frames how long crash-cooling is taking per batch so you can spot batches that are cooling slower than the normal process before it becomes annoying.
